families.name: Online Reciprocating Compressors (Mother & Online Stations)
families.summary: Multi-stage reciprocating compressors that take pipeline gas up to CNG storage pressure, for mother stations, online stations and pipeline boosting.
families.howItWorks:
A reciprocating compressor raises gas pressure in steps. Compressing natural gas from pipeline pressure to about 250 bar in one cylinder would produce very high temperatures, so the job is split across **several stages**, usually three or four for CNG. Each stage handles a similar pressure ratio.

An electric motor (or gas engine) drives a **crankshaft** directly or through belts. Connecting rods and crossheads turn the rotation into straight-line piston strokes. Each cylinder has automatic **suction and discharge valves** that open and close with the pressure difference. Gas is drawn in, compressed and pushed out on every stroke. Each stage has a smaller bore than the one before, because the gas becomes denser.

**Intercooling** follows each stage. The hot gas passes through an air-cooled (or water-cooled) heat exchanger to bring its temperature back down before the next stage. This cuts the power needed, protects valves and seals, and lets moisture or liquids drop out in **separators**, which drain automatically. An aftercooler cools the gas before it leaves the package.

In **non-lubricated** cylinders the piston and rider rings are made of self-lubricating polymers instead of oil-fed metal, so the gas leaves oil-free. Inlet filtration and a gas dryer protect the machine and the downstream vehicle cylinders. Each stage has a safety relief valve, and temperature, pressure and vibration trips are monitored by the control panel. At start and stop the machine is unloaded or blown down to a recovery vessel. Discharge goes to a priority panel and storage at an online station, or to filling posts for mobile cascades at a mother station.

families.name: Hydraulic Booster Compressors
families.summary: Compact, hydraulically driven compressors that draw gas from a mobile cascade and raise it to vehicle-filling pressure, the core of a daughter station.
families.howItWorks:
A hydraulic booster replaces the electric-motor crankshaft of a conventional compressor with **hydraulic drive**. An electric motor turns a hydraulic pump in a power unit. The pump drives a hydraulic piston back and forth, and that piston is rigidly connected to gas pistons in sealed compression cylinders. A directional valve reverses the oil flow at the end of each stroke, so gas is drawn in and pushed out on alternate strokes through check valves.

The booster is suited to cascade offloading because hydraulic drive works well with **variable suction pressure**. When a cascade arrives full (around 200 bar), the booster has little to do and its throughput is high. As the cascade empties, the compression ratio rises and the throughput falls, but the booster can keep drawing gas down to a low residual pressure. The suction range runs from 200 down to 30 bar g. The lower the cascade can be emptied, the more gas is sold per trip and the fewer truck deliveries are needed.

The gas end runs with **non-lubricated** seals, so no oil enters the gas. This protects dispensers and vehicle cylinders. The hydraulic oil is cooled by a fan cooler, and the gas may be cooled after compression before it reaches the dispenser or a small buffer store. A PLC sequences the strokes, monitors pressures and temperatures, and shuts the unit down on a fault. Boosters can also be connected to SCADA or RTU systems for remote monitoring.

families.name: Integrated CNG Station Solutions
families.summary: Complete station configurations (mother, online and daughter) built from compressors, storage, dispensers and controls, sized to your gas supply and vehicle demand.
families.howItWorks:
A CNG station takes natural gas at whatever pressure is available, compresses it to about **250 bar**, stores it and dispenses it into vehicle cylinders rated for **200 bar**. The supply source decides the configuration.

**Mother station.** Located on a gas pipeline. A large multi-stage reciprocating compressor fills mobile cascades (racks of high-pressure cylinders on a truck or trailer) through filling posts. It may also have dispensers for local vehicles.

**Online station.** Also connected to a pipeline, but it compresses gas only for its own dispensers. Gas goes from the compressor through a priority panel into stationary storage banks and on to the forecourt.

**Daughter station.** Has no pipeline. It gets gas from a mobile cascade trucked in from a mother station. At first the cascade's own pressure fills vehicles directly. As that pressure drops, a **hydraulic booster compressor** pushes the remaining gas up to dispensing pressure. This lets the station empty the cascade down to a low residual pressure before the truck returns for a refill.

Every configuration needs the same supporting systems: gas filtration and drying, **sequential (low/medium/high) bank filling** to keep fills fast and save compressor energy, emergency shutdown, gas detection, venting and fire protection.

In Nigeria, many new stations under the Presidential CNG programme are daughter stations, because pipeline access is limited. That makes the booster, cascade and dispenser set-up the most common station package.

faq.q: What is the difference between a mother, online and daughter station?
faq.a: Mother and online stations are both on a gas pipeline. A mother station mainly fills mobile cascades for other sites, while an online station compresses gas only for its own dispensers. A daughter station has no pipeline and runs on gas delivered by cascade.

faq.q: Why does a daughter station need a booster?
faq.a: As vehicles are filled, the cascade pressure falls and soon cannot fill a 200 bar vehicle cylinder by itself. The booster raises the remaining gas to dispensing pressure, so more of each delivery can be sold.

faq.q: Can a station be expanded later?
faq.a: Yes, if planned for. Leave space and pipework connections for extra storage, dispensers or a second compressor, and size the electrical supply with growth in mind.

faq.q: Do you supply vehicle conversion kits?
faq.a: This range covers station-side equipment. Vehicle conversion should be done at accredited conversion centres using certified kits and cylinders.

families.name: CNG Dispensers
families.summary: Metered CNG/CBG dispensers in 1 to 3 bank configurations for cars, buses and tricycles, with safety shut-offs and billing.
families.howItWorks:
A CNG dispenser does for gas what a petrol pump does for liquid fuel, but at about 200 bar into the vehicle. It has to measure accurately, fill quickly and stop at the right pressure.

**Metering.** Gas is sold by mass (kg) or standard volume, so most CNG dispensers use a **Coriolis mass-flow meter**. Gas flows through vibrating tubes, and the mass flow twists the tubes slightly. The meter turns that twist into mass flow regardless of pressure or temperature. The electronics multiply the result by the unit price for the display and billing.

**Sequential bank filling.** In a 2- or 3-bank dispenser, solenoid or electro-pneumatic valves fill first from the low-pressure storage bank. When flow drops, they switch to the medium bank and then to the high bank. This draws stored gas down evenly and keeps fills fast, and the compressor then tops up the banks.

**Temperature compensation.** Gas heats up as it is compressed into the vehicle cylinder. A cylinder filled to 200 bar while hot will settle below 200 bar once it cools. A temperature-compensated dispenser uses ambient temperature to calculate a target pressure that gives the correct settled fill without ever exceeding the cylinder's safe limit. This matters in Nigeria's high ambient temperatures.

**Safety.** Each hose has a **breakaway coupling** that separates and seals both ends if a vehicle drives off while connected. An over-pressure cut-off and excess-flow protection limit what reaches the vehicle. Filters remove particles and oil aerosols, and nozzles are designed to match standard vehicle receptacles.

faq.a: Gas volume changes with pressure and temperature. Mass is constant, so mass-based metering is fair to both buyer and seller.

faq.a: A coupling in the hose that separates and seals both ends if a vehicle drives away while still connected, preventing a gas release.

families.name: Cascades & Storage
families.summary: High-pressure cylinder banks that store compressed gas at the station or carry it by road to daughter stations, supplied as part of a station solution.
families.howItWorks:
A cascade is a group of high-pressure gas cylinders connected by manifold piping and valves. It is usually rated around **250 bar** and mounted in a steel frame. **Stationary** cascades stay on site as station storage. **Mobile** cascades are mounted on a truck or trailer and carry gas from a mother station to daughter stations or industrial users.

Station storage is normally split into **low, medium and high pressure banks**. A **priority panel** sends the compressor's output first to the dispensers when vehicles are filling, and otherwise to the banks in order, starting with the high bank. When dispensing, the dispenser draws from the low bank first and moves to higher banks as flow drops. Running the banks this way gives fast fills and uses more of the stored gas than a single bank could.

A mobile cascade is filled at a mother station through a filling post, then driven to the daughter site and connected to the booster through a decanting panel. Storage capacity is usually stated as **water volume** (litres). Multiplying water volume by the usable pressure drop gives the gas available.

Cylinders are made of steel or composite (Type 1 to 4), each with a valve, a burst disc or pressure relief device, and an individual certificate. They need periodic **inspection and hydrostatic retesting** to stay in service.

Chanrai supplies mobile and stationary cascades as part of a station package, sized to each project.

families.name: Gas Utility Skids (Metering, Pressure Regulating, Decompression)
families.summary: Pre-fabricated skids that measure gas, reduce and control its pressure, and decompress CNG for industrial and network users.
families.howItWorks:
Gas utility skids are factory-built assemblies of piping, valves and instruments on a steel base. They are made to be lifted into place and connected.

**Metering skids** measure gas for custody transfer or process control. The meter type depends on flow range and accuracy: rotary positive displacement (RPD) for low to medium flows, turbine or ultrasonic for larger and steadier flows, and orifice or vortex where simplicity matters. A **flow computer** corrects measured volume to standard conditions using pressure and temperature, totalises it and can send data to SCADA. A twin-stream design allows one meter to be serviced while the other stays in use.

**Pressure regulating skids (PRS)** reduce supply pressure to the level the user needs and hold it steady as demand changes. A typical stream has an isolation valve, filter, slam-shut valve, active regulator and monitor regulator. Pressure relief valves protect downstream equipment, and **fail-to-close** logic shuts off supply if control is lost. **Odorisation** is added where gas enters public distribution, so leaks can be smelled.

**Decompression skids** take gas from very high pressure (for example a CNG cascade at about 200 bar) down to usable pressure. A large pressure drop cools gas sharply (the Joule-Thomson effect), which can freeze regulators and form hydrates. A **hot-water bath or electric heater** warms the gas before or between reduction stages to prevent this.

choosingTips: Specify maximum and minimum flow (SCMH) and inlet/outlet pressure ranges, including the lowest inlet pressure.

Filter differential pressure

safety: Install with correct hazardous-area classification, earthing and ventilation, and secure the site against public access.
Keep relief valves and slam-shuts tested so that downstream equipment is never over-pressured.
Never bypass decompression heating. Frozen regulators can fail and lose control of pressure.
Gas supply installations are subject to Nigerian midstream and downstream regulation. Confirm approvals with the regulator and your gas supplier.

faq.q: Why does CNG decompression need heating?
faq.a: Gas cools sharply when its pressure is cut. Without heating, regulators can freeze and moisture can form ice or hydrates.

faq.q: Which meter should I use?
faq.a: It depends on flow range, accuracy and whether the meter is for billing. SPTL offers RPD, ultrasonic, turbine, orifice and vortex options.

faq.q: What is fail-to-close?
faq.a: A safety principle where the regulating system shuts off gas, rather than letting it through, if control is lost.

families.name: CNG Tube Trailer Skids
families.summary: Road-going skids of large high-pressure tubes that carry CNG from the mother station to consumers and to daughter stations in a virtual pipeline network.
families.howItWorks:
A **tube trailer skid** is a bank of long, large-diameter seamless pressure tubes held in a steel frame and connected by a manifold with isolation valves. The skid is mounted on a semi-trailer, or built as a container-sized frame that can be lifted onto one.

At the **mother station** the skid is connected to a filling post and filled by the station compressors. A truck then pulls it to the **daughter station** or to an industrial customer, where it is connected to a decanting panel. At a daughter station a booster compressor draws gas from the tubes and raises it to dispensing pressure; at an industrial site a pressure-reducing skid lowers it to the pressure the burners or engines need.

When the skid is nearly empty it is swapped for a full one and returned to the mother station. Moving gas this way is called a **virtual pipeline**: it reaches customers far from the gas network without building a pipeline.

keyComponents.role: Store compressed gas at working pressure, each built and certified for high-pressure service.

keyComponents.role: Connect the tubes and allow each one to be isolated.

keyComponents.role: Protect the tubes from overpressure or fire exposure.

keyComponents.role: Carry and protect the tubes on the road.

choosingTips: Size the skid's water volume from daily gas demand and how often deliveries can be made.
Allow for the residual pressure your booster or pressure-reducing skid can reach.
Confirm tube certificates, manufacture dates and next retest dates before acceptance.
Check road-vehicle compliance, axle loads and driver training for your routes.

dailyChecks: Visual check for damage, corrosion or leaks
Check valves and relief devices are not tampered with
Check tyres, lights and coupling before every trip
maintenance.note: Indicative. Tube requalification is set by calendar under the tube standard and the regulator, not by hours.

safety: Use only tubes manufactured, tested and certified to a recognised high-pressure gas standard, and keep the certificates.
Earth the skid during filling and decanting, and keep it away from ignition sources and public access.
Follow Nigerian regulations for transporting and storing compressed gas.

faq.q: What is a virtual pipeline?
faq.a: Moving compressed gas by road in tube trailer skids from a mother station to customers, instead of through a pipeline.

faq.q: How much gas does a tube trailer carry?
faq.a: It depends on water volume, working pressure and how far it can be emptied at the delivery point. Ask us to calculate it for your route and demand.
